data.name: Warning_TortoiseGitMissingKey_Title
data.value: A remote points at a key file that is gone

data.name: Warning_TortoiseGitMissingKey_Body
data.value: TortoiseGit has a remote bound to a PuTTY key that no longer exists on disk, so pushing to it will fail. Rebind the remote to a key you still have, or restore the file.

data.name: Warning_WslSeparateKeys_Title
data.value: A WSL distribution has its own SSH keys

data.name: Warning_WslSeparateKeys_Body
data.value: Keys inside a WSL distribution are a separate set from the ones in your Windows home directory. Work done inside the distribution uses these, which is easy to forget when a push suddenly stops working on one side.

data.name: Profiles_DryRun
data.value: Dry run — show changes without applying them

data.name: Profiles_NothingToDo
data.value: Everything is already as this profile wants it.

data.name: Profiles_ApplyDryRunFirst
data.value: Preview the changes before applying them.

data.name: Profiles_Applied
data.value: Applied. A snapshot was taken first, so this can be rolled back.

data.name: Repositories_NoRoots
data.value: Add a folder in Settings to search for repositories.

data.name: Settings_AutoHideSeconds
data.value: Hide a revealed secret after {0} s

data.name: Settings_DiagnosticsNote
data.value: Nothing is written until you have seen exactly what the bundle contains. Values from your Git configuration are never included, only the names of the settings.

data.name: Settings_TelemetryNone
data.value: GitVault collects nothing and makes no network calls.

data.name: Warning_KeyWorldReadable_Title
data.value: Private key is readable by others

data.name: Warning_KeyWorldReadable_Body
data.value: OpenSSH refuses to use a private key that other accounts on this machine can read. Set the file mode to 0600 so that only you can read it.

data.name: Warning_RsaTooShort_Title
data.value: RSA key is shorter than 3072 bits

data.name: Warning_RsaTooShort_Body
data.value: Short RSA keys no longer meet current guidance. Generate a new Ed25519 key, or an RSA key of at least 3072 bits, and replace this one on every host that trusts it.

data.name: Warning_DsaDeprecated_Body
data.value: DSA is disabled by default in current OpenSSH releases and will stop working. Replace it with an Ed25519 key.

data.name: Warning_KeyNoPassphrase_Body
data.value: Anyone who copies this file gets your access. Add a passphrase and load the key into an agent so you still type it only once per session.

data.name: Warning_OrphanedPublicKey_Title
data.value: Public key without a private key

data.name: Warning_OrphanedPublicKey_Body
data.value: A .pub file was found with no matching private key. Either the private key lives elsewhere, or it is held only by a hardware token or an agent.

data.name: Warning_PlaintextCredentialStore_Body
data.value: This store keeps passwords and tokens unencrypted on disk. Switch the credential helper to your operating system's vault.

data.name: Warning_MissingPublicKey_Title
data.value: No .pub file next to the private key

data.name: Warning_MissingPublicKey_Body
data.value: Several tools expect the public key to sit beside the private one. GitVault can write it: for an unencrypted key it derives it directly, and for a protected key it asks for the passphrase first.

data.name: Warning_KeyIntegrityFailed_Title
data.value: The key file failed its own integrity check

data.name: Warning_KeyIntegrityFailed_Body
data.value: A PuTTY key file stores a MAC over its own contents, and this one does not match. The file has been edited or damaged since it was written; do not rely on it until you have checked where it came from.

data.name: Warning_AgentNotRunning_Body
data.value: Keys cannot be held in memory while the agent is stopped, so you will be asked for the passphrase on every connection.

data.name: Warning_GitNotFound_Body
data.value: GitVault fell back to reading the configuration files itself. Conditional includes and platform path quirks are resolved less accurately than git would resolve them. Install git, or add it to PATH.

data.name: Warning_NoIdentityConfigured_Body
data.value: Neither user.name nor user.email is set anywhere, so git will refuse to create a commit. Set them globally, or per repository through a profile.

data.name: Options_SettingsOnlyNote
data.value: Editing these lists changes GitVault's own settings only. No repository, key or credential is modified.

data.name: Options_KeysReadOnlyNote
data.value: GitVault reads key files and never writes to them.

data.name: Options_PickScanRoot
data.value: Choose a folder to search for repositories

data.name: Options_PickKeyFolder
data.value: Choose a folder to search for SSH keys

data.name: Options_NoKeyFolders

data.name: Profiles_New_NoIdentities
data.value: No identity has been discovered yet. Run a scan first.

data.name: Profiles_Delete_Detail
data.value: This removes the profile only. No identity, key or credential is deleted, and nothing already applied is undone.

data.name: Profiles_SnapshotNote
data.value: A snapshot is created before any mutation, and Apply stays disabled until a dry-run plan has been reviewed.

data.name: Profiles_StoredScopeNote
data.value: The scope opens with the value saved on the profile rather than defaulting to Global.

data.name: Config_Subtitle
data.value: Every configuration value that reaches this repository, and the scope it came from.

data.name: Config_PreviewNote
data.value: Every edit is previewed before it is written, and the file it changes is copied aside first.

data.name: Config_SystemScopeNote
data.value: The system scope usually needs elevated privileges. GitVault will not elevate; if the write is refused it says so and changes nothing.

data.name: Project_Subtitle
data.value: What GitVault should assume about this repository.

data.name: Project_NoRepository
data.value: Select a repository in the tree to see its settings.

data.name: Project_StorageNote
data.value: These settings are stored in a [gitvault] section of this repository's own configuration, so they travel with the folder. Saving them is a write to .git/config and is previewed and snapshotted like any other.
